To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
QKI-5 and QKI-6 are novel RNA-binding proteins that are components of the RNA-induced silencing complex (RICS) and that QKI-7 is not a component of the RICS.
QKI-5 and QKI-6 bind Ago2 in a cell-type specific manner and that QKI- 6 co-localizes in stress granules with Ago2 and MBP mRNA.
QKI-1 and QKI-6 are components of the RNA induced silence complex (RISC) and QKI-1, QKI-5 and QKI-5 are components of stress granules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the QKI isoform proteins during stress granule assembly.
the role of QKI in glial cell development and function.
the role of the QKI isoform proteins in the formation of cytoplasmic RNA granules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QKI-5 and QKI-6 are both involved in the regulation of the MBP mRNA in oligodendroglial cells, and that the QKI-7 isoform is not expressed in these cells.
QKI-1 isoforms are involved in the regulation of mRNA metabolism and are involved in the formation and/or function of stress granules.
the QKI-1 isoforms are RNA binding proteins that are involved in regulating the stability of mRNAs in the cytoplasm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
QKI-7, QKI-5 and QKI-6 are involved in the control of mRNA metabolism in glial cells and that QKI-5 may play a role during cellular stress.
QKI-5 and QKI-6 are RNA binding proteins that regulate the expression of myelin basic protein mRNAs and localize to stress granules in response to stress.
QKI-1 and QKI-6 are involved in the regulation of RNA metabolism in stress granules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QKI-7 is the major QKI isoform expressed in oligodendroglial cells and that it is not expressed in astrocytes or neurons.
QKI-5 and QKI-6 are differentially expressed in oligodendroglial cells and have distinct roles in the regulation of RNA metabolism.
QKI proteins are likely to play a role in the formation of stress granules.
